string.text: What the hell is going on here? Another illusion? I need to find a psi-stabilizer.

1975. At one of the Kyiv institutes dealing with management problems, a modest Laboratory No. 15 is created, one of whose employees is listed as a certain Viktor Krivoshein. The goals of the laboratory are not disclosed.

All documents are stamped "Top Secret". All that is known is that the laboratory, modest in size, consumes more energy than the rest of the institute combined. To all questions, management responds that there is nothing special about the laboratory, and that the secrecy is merely a simple formality.
1986. A terrible catastrophe in Ukraine shakes the entire world. An accident at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, located 200 kilometers from Kyiv, has alarmed the public in earnest.

Unable to withstand the pressure, the government makes the decision to immediately evacuate children from the capital to avoid possible consequences. One of the creators of the Chernobyl reactor is found dead. The official verdict - suicide.

It is assumed that, confident in the indestructibility of his creation, he could not come to terms with the terrible catastrophe. According to official documents, the reactor exploded due to a failure to observe safety regulations, however the reason for the shutdown of the backup automatic safety systems has not been named by anyone.

Some sources claim that a scheduled maintenance was being carried out at the station, others - an unplanned experiment. The true causes of both the explosion and the academician's suicide remain unknown. The reactor is covered with a concrete sarcophagus, and the 30-kilometer territory surrounding it is named the "Chernobyl Exclusion Zone."

But nature takes its course, and the radiation levels gradually subside. 1996. Part of the local population displays unmotivated aggression. An organization calling itself the "Grey Brotherhood" seizes nearby towns. Attempts at a peaceful resolution of the conflict fail. The police uses force and detains the "grey zombies." Their further fate is unknown.

The head of the organization, as it turned out, is Viktor Krivoshein. A former employee of Laboratory No. 15, which by that time had completely ceased to exist, its staff having scattered in search of a better life. 2001. Mass excursions are organized into the zone. Tourists thirsting for thrills flock to the contaminated territory.

The first rumors appear about the instability of the sarcophagus and strange energy discharges occurring within the perimeter. But all public attention is riveted to other problems. A well-known journalist has disappeared. The investigation into his case reaches a dead end. For unknown reasons, the investigation did not move to examine the journalistic materials gathered by the missing man.

Also found dead is a general of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, under whose jurisdiction the Chernobyl zone fell. And once again the cause of death is suicide. The authorities and the mass media under their control attempt to hush up these events. After the general's death, the fate of the funds allocated for the elimination of the consequences of the accident remains unknown.
Television and newspapers are silent. Even the western media sidestep the issue. It remains unclear whether or not the funding promised by foreign partners was ever received.

2004. More and more rumors about anomalous activity on the territory of the Zone. Poorly understood energy discharges occur many times more frequently. There is still no information about what is happening inside the sarcophagus, packed with an enormous amount of nuclear fuel.

Whether this is the consequence of human negligence or the beginning of a secret experiment is unknown. 2005. A dark reputation grows around Pripyat. Strange animals appear on the nighttime streets of the dead city. The first reports of missing persons begin to come in.

2006. A bus carrying foreign tourists disappears in Pripyat. The decision is made to immediately close the Zone to visitors. Unsuccessful attempts are made to resettle people from the territories adjacent to the perimeter. The missing bus is never found, which causes no public outcry.

Everyone has already grown accustomed to the fact that the most high-profile cases go unsolved. Several days later, local residents bring the body of a strange animal to the checkpoint. The mutated creature has a humanoid build, small stature, and large black eyes.

Residents of the areas surrounding the closed zone complain of increasingly frequent underground tremors. In autumn, anomalous morning hurricanes begin. At around six in the morning a terrifying wind sweeps in, which a minute later instantly dies down, leaving behind uprooted trees and shattered windows.

2007. A blinding flash of white light of unknown origin illuminates the territory of the Zone. A moment later a terrible roar sounds and an earthquake begins. People run, fall to the ground, clutching their bleeding eyes and ears. Some manage to escape, others are evacuated by soldiers who have cordoned off the Zone along its entire perimeter.

2008. More and more people are drawn to the Zone. From adventurers of all stripes to scientists and military personnel. Despite the perimeter being guarded by special forces, on the black market one can increasingly encounter strange objects of anomalous origin. Strange and unpredictable.
And among the residents of the towns and villages bordering the Zone, a new profession emerges. Stalker.
Despite the intensifying crisis and the actions of certain destructive elements, all vital processes in the city remain under control.

Thus, in the financial sector, thanks to the support of the transnational company "Blatcol," it was even possible to introduce regular payments of allowances, pensions, and so on. However, the disbursement rates had to be somewhat reduced.

As of today, the monthly allowance for the average resident amounts to 2 kilograms of bread, 10 liters of drinking water, and 1 kilogram of meat. Naturally, it is still too early to speak of achieving the biological minimum.

The Cabinet of Ministers held an emergency session yesterday, at which the question of measures to suppress attempts by certain shady individuals to exploit the temporary economic difficulties being experienced by our country was discussed.

Riding a wave of openly populist aspirations that seek to channel the random, chaotic outbursts of certain unconscientious elements toward their own ends, certain irresponsible elements are persistently spreading rumors that a feverish construction of some sort of mythical labyrinths is allegedly underway beneath the metro lines.

This is likely connected to recent statements from the administration of the Kiev metro. We remind our listeners that the administration bears no responsibility for the lives of passengers who attempt to remain on metro grounds after its closure.

Certain unscrupulous journalists claim to possess some documents regarding the financing of a certain project under the laughable code name "Anthill." Despite all efforts undertaken by the Cabinet of Ministers, some isolated instability is nevertheless observed in certain sectors of our economy.

In connection with this, it became necessary to cut off the water and electricity supply to residential districts, but there are no real grounds for serious concern. These measures are only temporary. These are the decisive steps that had to be taken due to the irresponsible who took advantage of the temporary difficulties.

Radical changes await us, but in order to reach them, we must deal with these irresponsible elements that stand in the way of the future. Isolated cases of unmotivated cruelty have been observed on the streets of our cities.

The situation will soon be fully under control, and the relevant authorities are doing everything necessary to localize the random outbreaks of violence. There are no grounds for concern. We decisively reject all provocative statements.

We repeat, there are no grounds for panic. Understanding the full complexity of the moment in the life of our state, we must keep ourselves in hand and only render assistance to the city's law enforcement authorities.
